blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how businesses keep track of their financial health? The accounting equation is the foundation of financial accounting.

blocks.markdown: The accounting equation is a fundamental principle in accounting that represents the relationship between a company's assets, liabilities, and capital. It is expressed as: Assets = Capital + Liabilities.

blocks.title: Key Terms
blocks.text: Assets: Resources owned by a business. Liabilities: Obligations or debts owed to others. Capital: Owner's interest in the business.

blocks.markdown: Every transaction in accounting affects the accounting equation. For example, when a business takes a loan, its assets and liabilities both increase. This keeps the equation balanced.

blocks.title: Example of a Transaction
blocks.prompt: Consider a business that purchases office equipment worth ₦100,000 on credit.

steps.text: Identify the asset involved: Office equipment worth ₦100,000 is added to assets.
Identify the liability: Since it is on credit, liabilities increase by ₦100,000.
Check the equation: Assets increase by ₦100,000 and Liabilities increase by ₦100,000, keeping the equation balanced.

blocks.answer: The accounting equation remains balanced as both assets and liabilities increase by the same amount.

blocks.markdown: It's important to classify items correctly to maintain accurate records. Assets include cash, inventory, and property. Liabilities include loans and accounts payable. Capital refers to the owner's equity in the business.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Always ensure that your transactions keep the accounting equation balanced. Double-check your classifications of assets, liabilities, and capital.

points: The accounting equation is Assets = Capital + Liabilities.
Every transaction affects the equation but keeps it balanced.
Correct classification of financial items is crucial.
